The issue arises when dealing with the input string `'28/01/2014 21:00:00 +0100'`. 

The function tries to match this string against various formats, but ultimately fails to parse it correctly due to the presence of the '+0100' time zone offset at the end. This is because none of the specified regular expressions in the `format_expressions` list account for this specific format.

Consequently, the function falls back on using `email.utils.parsedate_tz`, which attempts to parse the date string using the RFC 2822 standard. However, when dealing with dates that include a time zone offset (e.g., '+0100'), this function can produce incorrect results or fail altogether.
